newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Fall in Japan Oct trade surplus to slow.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Fall in Japan Oct trade surplus to slow.

text.p: The pace of decline in Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus will slow in October from a year earlier on the back of a weaker yen or the surplus may even rise for the first time in 23 months, economists say.

Estimates given by economists polled by Reuters ranged from a surplus of 396 billion yen to 650 billion yen, against a surplus of 540.5 billion yen a year ago. The data is due to be released at 8.50 am on Monday (2350 GMT on Sunday). "The surplus may fluctuate from month to month. However, the general trend of the sharp drop turning milder hasn't changed," said Yasuhiko Ushikubo, an Industrial Bank of Japan economist.

Economists noted a sharp pick-up in automobile exports to Asia and the United States in October, as Japanese products recovered their global competitiveness with the weakening of the yen against the dollar.
Meanwhile, imports would have remained steady, due to good demand for oil, semiconductor parts, and communications and office equipment, they said.
Although the forecasts ranged from a slight increase to a mild drop in the trade surplus for October, many of the economists agreed the surplus would start expanding in the coming months.
"The increase in the trade surplus will come more as a result of a fall in imports rather than a rise in exports," said an economist at a foreign brokerage.
But even if the trade surplus starts expanding again, any increase would be small, the economists said.
Japanese companies have been moving their production overseas, which has contributed to fewer exports from Japan and more imports of their finished products into Japan.
Meanwhile, growth in imports will suffer from the weakness of the yen and slowing consumption in Japan, which may drop further with a rise in the consumption tax in April, they said.

Some economists say the weakness of the yen against the dollar will not change despite a possible rise in the trade surplus, while others say a rise in the surplus may strengthen the yen to around the 105 to 110 yen/dollar range.
